title: 2D Combat
description: Easy questions from the 2D combat course: dash, stamina, knockback, enemy AI, bullet patterns and your own Rage.

questions.context: PlayerController runs Dash() when you press the dash button. On the Player prefab moveSpeed is 4.
questions.prompt: While the dash lasts, how fast does the demon hunter move?
questions.hint: Look at the line with *= - it multiplies moveSpeed (4) by dashSpeed (4).
questions.explanation: moveSpeed *= dashSpeed makes 4 x 4 = 16. EndDashRoutine sets it back to startingMoveSpeed (4) when the dash ends.

questions.context: Dash() starts this coroutine right after it boosts moveSpeed. Dash() refuses to run while isDashing is true.
questions.prompt: How long is the speed boost, and when can you dash again?
questions.hint: Two waits in a row: the first one ends the boost, the second one ends isDashing.
options: Boost 0.2 s, next dash 0.25 s after the boost ends
Boost 0.45 s, next dash right away
Boost 0.25 s, next dash after 0.2 s
The boost lasts until you let go of the button
questions.explanation: After 0.2 s moveSpeed goes back to normal. isDashing stays true for another 0.25 s, so the next dash is possible 0.45 s after the first one started.

questions.context: Your stamina bar is a little more than half full: CurrentStamina = 0.6. You press dash.
questions.hint: CanDash compares CurrentStamina with dashCost. Is 0.6 >= 1?
options: Nothing - the dash does not happen
The dash happens and stamina goes below 0
The dash happens and costs health instead
questions.explanation: 0.6 >= 1 is false, so CanDash is false and the whole if is skipped: no stamina is used, no speed boost.

questions.context: You just used your last dash: CurrentStamina = 0. You pick up no stamina globe.
questions.prompt: About how long until you can dash again?
questions.hint: Time.deltaTime makes regenPerSecond really "per second". How many seconds of 1/3 does it take to reach dashCost 1?
options: Never - only a stamina globe refills it
questions.explanation: Each second adds 1/3 stamina, so after 3 seconds CurrentStamina reaches 1 = dashCost and CanDash is true again.

questions.context: You dash and the stamina bar in the UI drops. These are the two scripts involved.
questions.prompt: How does the stamina bar find out that stamina changed?
questions.hint: One script calls Invoke, the other one wrote += in OnEnable.
options: Stamina fires the OnStaminaChanged event, and StaminaBar, subscribed in OnEnable, runs UpdateBar
StaminaBar reads Stamina.Instance every frame in Update
Stamina finds the bar with GameObject.Find and sets its value
PlayerController updates the bar after each dash
questions.explanation: This is the Observer pattern: Stamina does not know the bar exists. It only fires OnStaminaChanged, and whoever subscribed (StaminaBar) reacts. OnDisable unsubscribes with -=.

questions.context: A Ghost bullet hits you. Half a second later a second bullet hits you too.
questions.prompt: How much health does the second bullet take?
questions.hint: What is canTakeDamage after the first hit, and when does it become true again?
questions.explanation: The first hit sets canTakeDamage = false for damageRecoveryTime (1 s). The second hit comes after 0.5 s, so TakeDamage returns at the first line.

questions.context: A slime hits you and the knockback starts. You keep holding the stick to run away.
questions.prompt: What does your input do during the knockback?
questions.hint: Look at the first line of Move(). What is GettingKnockedBack during the knockback?
options: Nothing - for 0.2 s you only slide where the hit pushed you
You steer the knockback in any direction
questions.explanation: While GettingKnockedBack is true, Move() returns before MovePosition. After knockBacktime (0.2 s) Knockback zeroes the velocity and your input works again.

questions.context: A slime touches you from your left side. PlayerHealth calls GetKnockedBack with the slime's transform.
questions.hint: transform.position - damageSource.position is an arrow from the slime to you.
options: To the right - away from the slime
To the left - towards the slime
questions.explanation: My position minus the source's position points from the slime to me. Normalized and multiplied by the thrust, it pushes me away from whatever hit me.

questions.context: Every enemy uses EnemyAI. The Slime prefab has attackRange = 0. You walk right up to a slime.
questions.prompt: Does the slime ever switch to State.Attacking?
questions.hint: Can a distance ever be smaller than 0?
options: No - it keeps Roaming; it only hurts you by touching you
Yes, as soon as it touches you
questions.explanation: A distance is never < 0, so the slime stays in Roaming. It still hurts you: PlayerHealth.OnCollisionStay2D calls TakeDamage when an EnemyAI touches the player.

questions.context: Before each burst the Ghost's Shooter works out a cone of bullets around you.
questions.prompt: How many degrees apart are two neighbouring bullets in one burst?
questions.hint: 8 bullets have 7 gaps between them. The code divides by (projectilesPerBurst - 1).
questions.explanation: 8 bullets from one edge of the 165° cone to the other leave 7 gaps: 165 / 7 = 23.57°. The first bullet flies at targetAngle - 82.5°, the last at targetAngle + 82.5°.

questions.context: With stagger on, the Ghost does not fire a whole burst at once - it sweeps the cone bullet by bullet.
questions.prompt: How often does a new bullet come out?
questions.hint: timeBetweenProjectiles = timeBetweenBursts / projectilesPerBurst. Put in 1 and 8.
options: Every 0.125 s - one burst takes 1 s
questions.explanation: 1 / 8 = 0.125 s between bullets, so the 8 bullets of a burst are spread over 1 second - the sweeping look of the Ghost.

questions.context: A Ghost bullet (isEnemyProjectile = true) flies through a bush.
questions.prompt: True or false: the bush breaks and drops loot.
questions.hint: The if needs the player's weapon (DamageSource) or a projectile that is NOT an enemy projectile.
questions.explanation: False. The bullet is a Projectile, but !projectile.IsEnemyProjectile is false, so the condition fails and the bush stays. Only your glaive, arrows and laser break bushes.

questions.context: DamageSource on your glaive calls TakeDamage with the glaive's weaponDamage. A slime starts with startingHealth 3.
questions.prompt: How many glaive hits does it take to kill a slime?
questions.hint: Each hit subtracts weaponDamage (1). When does currentHealth reach 0?
questions.explanation: 3 - 1 - 1 - 1 = 0, so the third hit kills it. The staff (weaponDamage 3) kills a slime in one hit.

questions.context: You start in Town and walk through a gate into Scene_1. Scene_1 has its own copy of the Player prefab, so it can also be started on its own.
questions.prompt: What happens to the Player that was placed in Scene_1?
questions.hint: When Scene_1's Player runs Awake, is instance already set?
options: It destroys itself - the Player from Town (DontDestroyOnLoad) carries on
It replaces the Player from Town
questions.explanation: The Player from Town already set instance and survived the scene load (DontDestroyOnLoad). Scene_1's copy finds instance != null and destroys itself.

questions.context: Scene_2 has two entrances. You leave Scene_1 through an exit whose sceneTransitionName is "Scene1_Exit".
questions.prompt: True or false: the player appears at the entrance whose transitionName is "Scene1_Exit".
questions.hint: Each AreaEntrance compares its own transitionName with the name the exit stored.
questions.explanation: True. Only the entrance with the matching name moves the player to itself. That is why entrance names must be unique in a scene.

questions.context: Your own Rage system. You start with 0 Rage, kill a slime with 3 glaive hits and do not get hit yourself.
questions.prompt: How much Rage do you have now?
questions.hint: Each of the 3 hits calls RegisterEnemyHit, and the kill calls RegisterKill once.
questions.explanation: 3 hits x 3 = 9, plus 5 for the kill = 14. Getting hit yourself would add 10 more.
